fields.sceneBrief: Phone snapshot taken from the riverbank looking at the downstream concrete pier of the Route 38 highway bridge over the swollen Cedar River at Cedar Ford, Iowa. A painted white-and-black river staff gauge runs up the pier face, and fast brown floodwater carrying small branches sits just below the 15-foot mark. To the right in the middle distance, a low dip in a two-lane county road beside a flooded boat ramp and park lot is covered by a thin sheet of muddy water, and a gray pickup truck is driving through it, throwing a small spray. An orange barricade trailer is parked far off at a side street, its barricades still loaded on it. It is early morning under a flat overcast sky with light drizzle, wet concrete, cold diffuse light, and the edge of the frame is slightly tilted as if held by someone in rain gear.
fields.caption: Staff gauge 14.9 at 07:17. Water is across the low dip on River Road by the boat ramp, about 2 inches deep, and two pickups just went through it. Attached: USGS real-time page, Cedar River at Cedar Ford (CFDI4), shows gage height 14.81 ft at 07:00 CDT, provisional data subject to revision, with no update since 07:00.

instructorNote: This is a field-over-screen clue. The staff gauge at 07:17 is 0.1 ft below flood stage and ahead of the USGS value from 07:00, and River Road south of Mill Street is already wet and still open. Watch for three things: PW confirms the barricades are set now, EM logs both readings with their times and sources, and the PIO is told to quote the measured stage with its time and source rather than the 14.81 shown on the screen.

Early morning, flat overcast sky, light drizzle, wet concrete, cold diffuse light, frame slightly tilted, candid handheld feel.
